pamphlet_excerpts: Lightning Evacuation Protocol: Sirens mandate instant clearing of fairways to reach designated grounded lightning storm shelters.
Heat Exhaustion Response: Move overheated players into shaded areas while loosening garments and providing cool water.
Blister Prevention Strategy: Friction on walking heels requires prompt application of adhesive moleskin patches before irritation.
Severe Weather Stance: Avoid isolated tall trees and metal flagsticks during rapid thunderstorm development on fairways.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Sound Assessment: Check local course weather sirens and scan horizon clouds before teeing off.
Step 2 - Shelter Relocation: Evacuate exposed hilltops immediately and enter fully enclosed clubhouses or maintenance sheds.
Step 3 - Equipment Grounding: Drop metal clubs and golf bags far away from your direct location.
Step 4 - Physical First Aid: Administer water and apply cold packs to soothe acute golfer heat cramps.

misconception_pool.misconception: Golf carts provide complete protection from lightning strikes during sudden thunderstorms on open fairways.
misconception_pool.fact: Golf carts lack rubber enclosed insulation and offer zero protection against direct lightning strikes.

misconception_pool.misconception: Standing under a tall tree on the fairway provides safe protection from lightning until the rain passes.
misconception_pool.fact: Isolated trees attract lightning strikes; golfers must move to an enclosed building or lightning shelter and drop their metal clubs.

misconception_pool.misconception: Popping a friction blister on your hand or heel with a tee lets you keep swinging without discomfort.
misconception_pool.fact: Puncturing an intact blister invites bacterial infection; cover the hot spot or blister with moleskin or a sterile adhesive bandage.

misconception_pool.misconception: Scrubbing skin with hot water and harsh soap hours after retrieving a ball from poison ivy prevents a rash.
misconception_pool.fact: Hot water opens pores and spreads urushiol oil; rinse exposed skin immediately with cool water and mild soap or rubbing alcohol.

misconception_pool.misconception: Walking off a freshly sprained ankle across the remaining holes keeps the joint loose and speeds up recovery.
misconception_pool.fact: Continuing to bear weight worsens ligament damage; stop playing and apply rest, ice, compression, and elevation right away.

children.pamphlet_summary: Short Iron Descending Strike Technique: Short irons utilize a centered ball position and an upright swing plane to strike the ball on a crisp descending path. pamphlet_excerpts: Short Iron Descending Strike Technique: Short irons utilize a centered ball position and an upright swing plane to strike the ball on a crisp descending path. common_misconception_pair.fact: Crisp short iron trajectory comes from striking down through the ball before taking a divot ahead of the lie.

A golfer selects the appropriate short game shot based on lie condition, pin distance, and green obstacles (p. 38).

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option A, Traditional Golf. Do ALL of the following: (1) Study the USGA Rules of Golf now in use. (a) Tell about the three categories of golf etiquette. (b) Demonstrate that you understand the definitions of golf terms. (c) Show that you understand the Rules of Amateur Status. (2) Tell about your understanding of the World Handicap System. (3) Do the following: (a) Tell about the early history of golf. (b) Describe golf's early years in the United States. (c) Tell about the accomplishments of a top golfer of your choice. (4) Do the following: (a) Tell how golf can contribute to a healthy lifestyle, mentally and physically. (b) Tell how a golf exercise plan can help you play better. Show two exercises that would help improve your game. (5) Show the following: (a) The proper grip, stance, posture, and key fundamentals of a good swing (b) Driver played from a tee (c) The fairway wood shot (d) The long iron shot (e) The short iron shot (f) The approach, chip-and-run, and pitch shots (g) A recovery shot from a bunker or heavy rough (h) A sound putting stroke (6) Play a minimum of two nine-hole rounds or one 18-hole round of golf with another golfer about your age and with your counselor, or an adult approved by your counselor. Do the following: (a) Follow the Rules of Golf. (b) Practice good golf etiquette. (c) Show respect to fellow golfers, committee, sponsor, and gallery. misconception_pool.misconception: Golf etiquette rules are optional informal recommendations that carry no competitive penalty points.
misconception_pool.fact: Breaching etiquette standards can result in disqualification or stroke penalties under official governing rules.

misconception_pool.misconception: Prying up the center of a pitch mark on the putting green with a tee is the proper way to level the turf.
misconception_pool.fact: Lifting the center tears grass roots and kills the turf; push grass inward from the outer edges and tap the surface flat with a putter.

misconception_pool.misconception: Golfers have five full minutes under the current USGA Rules of Golf to search for a ball in the rough before it is lost.
misconception_pool.fact: The USGA Rules of Golf limit a ball search to three minutes from when the player or their caddie begins looking for it.

misconception_pool.misconception: A golfer's net score on a hole is the total number of strokes taken plus any penalty strokes before applying a handicap.
misconception_pool.fact: Total strokes plus penalties equals the gross score, whereas the net score subtracts the player's handicap strokes from the gross score.

misconception_pool.misconception: Amateur golfers cannot accept any retail merchandise prize or trophy in a tournament without losing their amateur status.
misconception_pool.fact: USGA Rules allow amateurs to accept non-cash prizes and even cash up to the current thousand-dollar limit in scratch competitions.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During an 18-hole round of traditional golf, your tee shot lands deep in a wooded area and you worry it may be lost. Under USGA Rules of Golf, what is the maximum time allowed to search for your ball before it is declared lost, and what may you play from the tee to save time?
options: 3 minutes search time; play a provisional ball before leaving the teeing area
10 minutes search time; drop a new ball at the nearest fairway edge with no penalty
5 minutes search time; take a free drop wherever your playing partner estimates it landed
1 minute search time; replay the hole from the tee with a two-stroke penalty only after walking back
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: Option A - 3 minutes search time; play a provisional ball before leaving the teeing area
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Under USGA Rule 18.2 and Rule 18.3, a player has 3 minutes to search for a ball once reaching the search area and may play a provisional ball before walking forward to maintain pace of play.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Your ball lies buried in a greenside sand bunker 15 yards from the pin. How should you set up your sand wedge and where should the clubhead enter the sand on a standard greenside bunker explosion shot?
options: Close the clubface, lean weight on the back foot, and strike the top half of the golf ball cleanly
Open the sand wedge clubface slightly, dig your feet in for stability, and splash the sand 2 inches behind the ball
Ground the clubhead firmly in the sand behind the ball during your practice address and chip with locked wrists
Use a putter from a deep lip bunker to roll the ball up a vertical grass face
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: Option B - Open the sand wedge clubface slightly, dig your feet in for stability, and splash the sand 2 inches behind the ball
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Greenside bunker shots use the bounce of an open sand wedge entering the sand about 2 inches behind the ball so a cushion of sand lifts the ball onto the green without touching the sand at address.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: While playing a PDGA Disc Golf round in a multi-use public park, a family with young children walks onto the fairway near the basket on a blind dogleg hole. Under PDGA Rule 812 (Courtesy), what must your group do?
options: Shout 'Fore!' while throwing your driver so they know to duck out of the way
Post a spotter ahead and wait to throw until all park pedestrians and prior players are completely clear of the landing zone
Skip the hole without recording a score and move to the next tee pad immediately
Throw a heavy putter instead of a distance driver so the impact will be softer
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: Option B - Post a spotter ahead and wait to throw until all park pedestrians and prior players are completely clear of the landing zone
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: PDGA Rule 812 and the Disc Golf Code require players never to throw into a blind area or when pedestrians or other players are within reach; always post a spotter and yield to park users.
